title: Windowed batch shaper and kernel planner for lower tail latency
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a windowed batching strategy combined with a kernel cost planner that proactively selects execution kernels and attention micro-optimizations to reduce tail latency under mixed token-length workloads. The approach groups incoming requests into short, tenant-aware time windows and uses a lightweight cost model to decide: (1) whether to admit into the current batch, (2) whether to route to a low-latency kernel variant, and (3) whether to apply attention pruning/fast-attn path for long-context requests. This ticket covers design, implementation, integration with KV cache, and canary rollout. The goal is to improve p95/p99 latency without materially decreasing throughput or increasing cost per token.
acceptance_criteria: p95 generation latency reduced by >=25% on mixed workloads compared to baseline (measured on staging cluster)
p99 not regressed more than 10% during 1h soak under synthetic bursty traffic
Throughput measured in tok/s maintained within -5% of baseline for steady-state load
Feature gated and toggleable per-tenant via config in orchestration layer
Fallback path to legacy continuous-batcher enabled and tested
End-to-end integration tests cover kernel switch correctness and kv-cache consistency
tasks: Design cost model for kernel selection (CPU/GPU time estimate, memory pressure, kv-cache hit impacts)
Implement time-window admission controller with tenant fairness and per-route SLO weights
Add kernel planner service that exposes candidate kernel scores and switch heuristics
Integrate attention micro-optimizations (blocked/strided attention and early-exit heuristics) as kernel flags
Ensure prefill/decode sequencing maintains KV cache invariants during kernel switches
Add telemetry: kernel_switch_rate, window_fill_ratio, queued_time_quantiles, per-tenant tail latency
Create bench harness scenarios (1: many short requests, 2: mixed short+long, 3: bursty tail-heavy)
Implement feature flag and rollout plan in deployment tooling
Write e2e tests and perf regression tests
Canary rollout and 72h soak on dedicated-dev cluster
progress_updates: 2026-02-21 — Kickoff with serving runtime and infra. Agreed window size initial default = 8ms, configurable per-tenant.
2026-02-25 — Prototype of windowed admission controller implemented; basic tenant fairness working. Microbench shows window fill ratio ~0.68 on mixed arrivals.
2026-03-03 — Kernel cost model v0: linear model combining token_count, seq_len, and observed kernel latency samples. Early eval indicates correct preference for low-latency kernel at short sequences.
2026-03-07 — Integrated attention fast-path flag (blocked attention) behind kernel planner. Observed 10-14% p95 improvement in isolated tests for long-context synthetic traces.
2026-03-10 — Identified KV cache invalidation edge-case when swapping kernel mid-decode for same request; added ordering guard and replay prevention (PR linked).

2026-03-12 — Began canary rollout to 5% of traffic on dedicated-dev; dashboards show p95 improving but p99 spikes during a specific burst pattern. Root cause under investigation (task: refine admission throttling for tail bursts).
engineering_notes: Trade-offs considered: larger windows improve batching efficiency but increase admission latency. Settled on small default windows (4–12ms) and an adaptive mode that grows windows under low load.

Kernel planner currently runs synchronously in admission path; this keeps decision latency bounded but increases CPU overhead. Consider moving to async scoring with short-circuit cache for frequent patterns.
Attention micro-optimizations show varying gains across model families; we gate by model profile (only enable for encoder-decoder and decoder-only models where blocked-attn is validated).
Cost model needs continuous calibration; plan to log prediction residuals and feed into nightly retraining job.
We intentionally avoid changing batching semantics for request-level isolation (no per-request partial execution) to keep correctness simple.

Observed interplay between windowed batching and autoscaler: if average windowing increases latency slightly under low load, autoscaler may scale down nodes incorrectly. Added autoscaler hint metric (expected_processing_latency) to mitigate.
performance_benchmarks: Baseline (mixed 1–8k tokens, staging): p95 = 380ms, p99 = 820ms, throughput = 250 tok/s/node
Windowed batcher + kernel planner (staging, same load): p95 = 285ms (–25%), p99 = 740ms (–9.8%), throughput = 245 tok/s/node (–2%)
With attention fast-path enabled for long sequences: p95 = 220ms (–42%), p99 = 680ms (–17%), throughput = 260 tok/s/node (+4%)
Cost estimate: effective cost/token reduced ~6% in the mixed workload due to higher cache reuse and more efficient kernels.
decisions: Use tenant-aware windows instead of pure global time windows to preserve fairness and avoid noisy neighbors.
Default kernel planner to prefer low-latency kernel for sequences < 512 tokens unless throughput SLO explicitly prioritized by tenant.
Gate attention micro-optimizations per-model with feature flags; enable by default on models with validated accuracy preservation.
Fallback behavior: if kernel switching causes >5% error rate or cache miss anomalies, auto-disable planner and revert to legacy batcher for the tenant.
Canary rollout plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 24–72h soak windows and automated rollback on SLO regression alerts.
blockers: Need final signoff from model-ops on attention fast-paths for customer-facing models (accuracy validation) — assigned to @model-ops
Autoscaler interaction causing spurious downscales during low-load windows; infra to implement expected_processing_latency metric (ENG-46782)
Perf harness needs additional traffic profiles from production traces (privacy-sanitized) — privacy team coordinating export
